content.comment_body: When I attempt to connect to my controller with [product_name] using my laptop, I encounter an error message. My system is Windows 7 Enterprise 64-bit and I'm using [product_name] [version_no]. I've already tried updating Java. The attached screenshot shows the error.

The error message suggests that you're trying to run a 64-bit DLL on a 32-bit operating system, but you've mentioned having Windows 7 64-bit. How did you install [product_name] [version_no]? Was it directly from the installation media or as an upgrade from a previous version?
I had the software on another PC and transferred it to my current one using a USB flash drive.
What exactly did you transfer from the other PC?
I can still use my other computer, so it's not a major issue. The folder I transferred is the software directory.
You can't simply copy an installed software directory to a different computer, as that won't result in a proper installation. You need to use the original installation media.
Here's a solution: go to this link and download [product_name] [version_no]. [url]
Your suggestion is not valid. Downloading the upgrade won't help without a full licensed version. A full version requires an original installation or original installation media.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered a major issue when attempting to run [product_name] [version_no] after moving installation files between computers via USB. The main problem was an error about running a 64-bit DLL on a 32-bit system, though the user's OS was Windows 7 64-bit. This confusion was due to not following a standard installation process, preventing effective software use. Users want intuitive, error-free installation and upgrade experiences.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to move and use [product_name] software easily between computers, with the ability to run the program after copying files, and clear error messages to support troubleshooting.
